title: Datacenter GPU Siting Scenarios — Power Attenuation & Thermal Headroom Study (Mar 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This working memo captures scenarios for colocating on-prem GPU pools (mixed A100/H100 chassis) across two representative datacenter shells: a 480V US colocation (pod A) and a 400V EU site (pod B). Primary focus: end-to-end power attenuation across PDUs and busways, rack-level thermal headroom with cold-aisle containment retrofit, and physical slotting options that reduce PDU imbalance and minimize disruptive cable rework during ramp.

Intended audience:
Platform engineering, SRE, data-center ops teams, and Site Reliability partners for customer on-prem installs. This is an iterative planning artifact — contains field questions and open action items.

Summary findings (high level):
- Long PDU runs (>12m) with mixed 3-phase delta/ wye conversions in our EU landlord rooms produce measurable voltage drop (~2.5–3.0% under full load) that pushes real power at the rack PDU inlet ~4–6% below nameplate. That increases current draw on upstream breakers and shrinks headroom margins when we assume nameplate GPU wattage.
- Cold-aisle containment retrofits in pod B recover ~8–12% thermal headroom at the top of rack vs. baseline open-aisle; however, aisle containment exacerbates hot-spoting when cable density in vertical rear channel exceeds 3U equivalent.
- Mixed-population slotting (interleaving H100 and A100) reduces peak per-rack draw variance by ~15% compared to grouping all high-power GPUs together. This is a strong operational lever to avoid local breaker trips.

Assumptions and baseline constants used in calculations:
- H100 (consensus sustained draw): 700W per GPU at nominal perf-per-watt profile (sustained batch), peak 750W transient.
- A100 sustained: 350W (sustained), peak 400W.
- Chassis: 8x H100/8x A100 appliance density options considered; chassis PDU overhead + management = 125W.
- Rack PDU rating: dual PDUs per rack, each 32A @ 208V (US) or 32A @ 230V (EU) circuit; however some EU rooms are 63A busway segments.
- Ambient inlet target: 20–24°C for H100 heavy pods; target max exhaust 45°C before throttling policies engage.

Power attenuation and feeder modeling (notes):
- Method: per-run voltage drop estimate = I * R_estimated over copper length, with I computed from expected rack load. Converted to power delta at rack: P = V_drop * I. We applied a conservative conductor resistance value from landlord MOPs for 4x10mm2 copper runs.
- Example: 10m feeder, expected rack current 90A, estimated V_drop ~2.2% (on 480V system) => P_loss ~95W per phase, cumulative ~285W across 3-phase. For a rack drawing 5kW, that is a ~5.7% loss margin.
- Implication: our published per-GPU power budgets (sustained) must include a feeder-loss buffer of at least 6% in long-run colocations, or we shift to shorter taps / higher-gauge busway.

Thermal headroom planning:
- Measured vs modeled: CFD samples from pod A show thick cable bundles routed in the rear increased exhaust temp delta by +2.8°C when bundle occupied >50% of vertical cable channel.
- Cold-aisle containment recommended when top-of-rack exhaust <45°C at baseline; containment combined with variable-speed CRAH control recovers ~8–12% extra rack capacity (modeled as tolerating an additional 300–600W per rack without exceeding exhaust threshold).
- Acceptance criteria for containment deployment:
  * Continuous vertical cable chase usage <= 40% planned; else run cable in underfloor trays where available.
  * CRAH staging control integrated with Redwood telemetry (Prometheus alert INF-CRAH-03).

Slotting & placement heuristics (operational rules):
- Rule A (spread high-power units): do not place more than 2 H100-equivalent chassis on consecutive racks served by the same dual-PDU bus section. Distribute across at least 4 separate PDU feeds where possible.
- Rule B (balance per PDU): use odd-even pairing for chassis PDUs — chassis pdu-A -> rack pdu-1, chassis pdu-B -> rack pdu-2, alternate on adjacent racks to avoid phase stacking on the feeder.
- Rule C (cable density guardrails): plan cable bundles so that rear vertical channel occupancy <= 50% for racks with >12kW nominal draw. Anything above this requires passive rear baffles or vertical exhaust fans.

Operational checklist (pre-install):
1) Obtain landlord single-line electrical drawing and conductor lengths for each rack cluster; verify with meter read of sample branch. (owner: Aisha P.)
2) Schedule thermography sweep after initial power-on + 72 hours sustained load. Flag any >10°C anomaly at busway tap points. (owner: Liam C.)
3) Confirm CRAH control points and setpoint integration with Redwood telemetry (scrub INF-CRAH-03). (owner: S. Martinez)
4) Prepare spare PDU/cable kits: two 63A bus taps and four 32A NEMA connectors per pod for fall-back. (owner: ops)
5) Check floor loading: any contiguous 6-rack block with combined cabinet equipment >5,500kg needs slab certification. (owner: Morgan R.)

Open questions / decisions required:
- Landlord constraints: pod B landlord only allows 4" raised floor void in legacy rooms (insufficient underfloor for new cable trays). Do we proceed with vertical bundles (requires more containment) or negotiate civil works? Impact: if we keep vertical bundles the thermal penalty increases and reduces usable rack capacity by ~10%.
- PDU vendor choices: do we standardize on busway taps (faster to commission) vs. dedicated 63A breaker drops (higher up-front civils)? Budget impact analysis requested. (linked Jira: INFRA-842)
- Onsite test plan: need to agree on the acceptance sustained load window (72h vs 7d). Engineering prefers 72h; SRE leaning to 7d for durability.

Short-term mitigation options (if landlord civils delayed):
- Enforce conservative slotting, keep high-power chassis spaced every 3 racks and limit sustained concurrency to 60% of rated throughput using rate-limiter at routing layer.
- Use automatic per-cabinet thermal throttling (via our runtime) to shed bulk-batch jobs if exhaust exceeds 44°C. This preserves reliability but impacts unit cost/KPU.

Commissioning test cases (minimal):
- T1: Incremental rack ramp: power to 25% of planned per-rack load -> 50% -> 75% -> sustained 100% for 72h. Record PDU inlet, busway temps, CRAH duct delta, and per-unit clock throttling events.
- T2: Cable-bundle worst-case: simulate bundle at 80% occupancy and run 72h sustained load at 80% nominal to identify hot-spots.
- T3: PDU failover: kill PDU-A at mid-load and observe automatic routing fallback and latency/reliability impact on a synthetic batch workload.

Notes from field visits (Mar 01–07):
- Pod A (US colocation) had several historical cases of 32A breaker trips in contiguous rack groups after a customer packed high-density storage gear. We recommend a site rule to cap per-rack sustained at 10kW without explicit ops signoff.
- Pod B (EU) landlord provided busway that simplifies future expansion but measured busway tap screw terminations were loose on two samples — immediate remedial torque check recommended.

Next steps and owners (short list):
- Finalize feeder-loss buffer policy and publish in colocation playbook (owner: Morgan R.; due 2026-03-22).
- Create a short runbook for slotting rules to hand to field teams and partners (owner: Andre D.; due 2026-03-19).
- Convene decision meeting about acceptance window (72h vs 7d) with SRE/product/ops (lead: Aisha P.; meeting target 2026-03-18).

Appendix: quick calculations (examples)
- Rack X, expected draw = 5.2kW. Estimated feeder loss (10m) = 300W => effective delivered = 4.9kW -> need to either shorten tap or derate by 6%.
- Four-rack block peak aggregate = 22kW -> if served by single 63A bus segment, margin to next bus tap = ~18% at 230V. If we group two H100 chassis adjacent, margin drops to ~6% (high trip risk).

Questions for review (call-out):
- Is platform comfortable with adding an explicit 6% feeder-loss buffer in all published rack power specs?
- Are we OK enforcing the 50% vertical cable occupancy guardrail on contracted installs?

Document history / revision notes:
- 2026-03-08: initial draft and site visit notes (Morgan R.).
- 2026-03-12: added feeder-loss calculations and slotting heuristics (Aisha P.).
- 2026-03-15: added commissioning steps and updated CRAH integration checklist (Liam C.).

(End of memo)
